commons:141487632.summary: In this small Romanesque carving the Virgin sits upright and frontal, one hand raised, with the Christ Child seated on her lap before her. The large, solemn faces and simple, block-like forms are typical of rural Romanesque images of Mary as the throne of her Son. It is kept in the parish church of La Alberca, in the province of Salamanca.
facts: The carving stands in the altarpiece of Saint Anne in the parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción at La Alberca, Salamanca.
The Commons photographer describes it as a Romanesque carving of the 11th–12th century.
commons:141487632.notes: The only source found is the Commons description; the date and material are not confirmed by a published catalogue. 'Painted wood' is inferred from the polychrome surface visible in the photograph.
commons:141487632.original_title: Nuestra Señora de las Majadas Viejas

cur:monumental-tokali-baptism.summary: Against the intense lapis-blue ground, John the Baptist at the left reaches out to lay his hand on the head of Christ, who stands frontally in the water of the Jordan, his haloed head inscribed IC XC. The painting's monumental heads and deep colour show the 'metropolitan' quality of the finest Cappadocian painting.
facts: Tokalı Kilise ('Church of the Buckle'), the largest church at Göreme, comprises an Old Church of the 10th century, painted in strips of red and green, and a larger New Church of the late 10th or early 11th century whose walls are dominated by rich indigo blue made from lapis lazuli.

Wikipedia notes that the lapis lazuli used in the New Church alone has been estimated as worth some 31.5 pounds of gold; the donors are often thought to have been the Phokas family, though without firm evidence.

cur:monumental-tokali-baptism.notes: The photograph shows a detail of the wall; whether the scene belongs to the Old or the New Church is not stated in the source. Dates for both phases are debated (c. 910s–920s for the Old Church; mid-10th to early 11th century for the New).
